pieces.name: ai-inventory
pieces.summary: Inventory AI systems and the controls around their use.
signals: Model or provider SDK imports and concrete model identifiers
Agent, prompt, retrieval, evaluation or human-oversight code
User-facing generative or decision-support features
inspect: Tracked dependency manifests and application source
Agent, prompt, retrieval and evaluation directories
User-facing notices near AI-backed interactions
pieces.caveat: An SDK dependency alone does not prove that an AI system is deployed; cite actual call sites and report uncertainty.

pieces.name: audit-pack
pieces.summary: Assemble audit scope, samples, workpapers and local evidence for one audit window.
signals: A named audit framework and review window
Population exports, sampling inputs or workpaper directories
A request to prepare an auditor handover
inspect: Local audit artifacts and population files
Existing reviewed .noru manifests that may form pack inputs
Noru evidence context for the named audit scope
pieces.caveat: Repository files cannot establish the audit framework, period or testing conclusion; obtain those from the user and Noru.

pieces.name: change-control
pieces.summary: Account for authorship, approval, merge and deployment separation over a change window.
signals: A repository hosted on a supported forge
Pull-request, review, merge and deployment history
A request about change management or segregation of duties
inspect: Repository remotes and CI deployment configuration
Credentialed forge history and branch-protection settings
The user-specified review window
pieces.caveat: The working tree cannot prove who approved or deployed a change; classify this as possibly relevant until forge history is available.

pieces.name: dev-agents
pieces.summary: Record the coding agents, MCP servers and plugins the development process depends on as reviewed suppliers.
signals: A committed .mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json or .gemini/settings.json
An agent-change-control manifest, or changes authored by coding agents
A request about which AI coding tools or MCP servers engineering depends on
inspect: Tracked agent configuration files, by server name, command name or host only
The acc manifest at .noru/.cache/acc-manifest.json, when acc runs here
Noru vendors and controls needed to decide suppliers and evidence links
pieces.caveat: A hostname or package scope is not a publisher, so a person decides every supplier; never read env, headers, args or URLs from a configuration file, and never count agent use per person.

pieces.name: evidence-push
pieces.summary: Match local artifacts to Noru's unmet evidence queue and upload reviewed files.
signals: Local reports, certificates, screenshots or signed records intended as evidence
A named control, framework or unmet evidence request
A request to file an artifact already held locally
inspect: The local artifacts the user placed in scope
Noru's current evidence queue for the named control or framework
Existing evidence records needed to avoid duplicates
pieces.caveat: A file's presence does not show that Noru needs it or that it satisfies an expectation; ask Noru and require human interpretation.

pieces.name: findings-ingest
pieces.summary: Turn SARIF and OSV-Scanner results that never reach a forge alert store into reviewed security findings.
signals: A committed .noru/findings-ingest.inputs.json
CI that writes SARIF or OSV-Scanner JSON as a build artifact without uploading it anywhere
Scanner configuration such as osv-scanner.toml or a SAST step whose results are not tracked
inspect: CI workflow steps that run scanners and where their reports are written
Whether any report is uploaded to a forge alert store
Noru risks, treatment due dates, assets and existing findings needed to interpret results
pieces.caveat: A report that also reaches a forge alert store is already importable and must not be ingested twice; a scanner result is a candidate finding, not a conclusion.

pieces.name: governance-records
pieces.summary: File attributed records of governance decisions and assigned actions.
signals: Board, committee, management-review or steering minutes
ISMS scope, statement of applicability or internal-audit records
Corrective-action plans or governance decisions held locally
inspect: Tracked governance and audit-document directories
Named participants, dates, decisions and action owners
Noru's unmet evidence expectations for the record
pieces.caveat: Do not infer that a meeting occurred, a decision was approved or an action was owned when the record does not say so.

pieces.name: iac-scan
pieces.summary: Find compliance-relevant misconfiguration in infrastructure and pipeline configuration.
signals: Terraform or CloudFormation infrastructure definitions
Kubernetes resource manifests
CI or deployment workflow configuration
inspect: Tracked infrastructure-as-code files
Kubernetes manifests and CI workflow directories
Noru assets, risks and existing findings needed to interpret results
pieces.caveat: A static rule match is a candidate finding, not a conclusion; the environment and an owner still have to be established.

pieces.name: privacy-datamap
pieces.summary: Build a privacy data map from the records and interfaces a repository defines.
signals: SQL DDL, migrations or ORM model definitions
Protobuf or GraphQL record schemas
Fields that appear to describe people, identifiers or their activity
inspect: Tracked schema, model, migration and API-contract files
Coverage markers for schema formats the collector cannot parse
Noru's privacy taxonomy and existing data-source map
pieces.caveat: Field names support classification but do not establish purpose, lawful basis or actual production use; those remain human decisions.

pieces.name: review-signoff
pieces.summary: Turn a completed periodic review of machine output into an expiring human sign-off.
signals: Access, firewall, hardening, asset, physical-access or vendor review exports
A recurring review cadence and review period
A named reviewer, outcome and owned exceptions
inspect: The review input and reconciliation output
Review dates, cadence, reviewer identity and exception owners
Noru's evidence queue for the relevant review
pieces.caveat: An export is not a sign-off; require the named human decision, review date, scope and expiry.

pieces.name: threat-model
pieces.summary: Turn a committed Open Threat Model into owned, expiring risks linked to the organization's controls.
signals: A committed *.otm.json threat model
Architecture or security review documents that describe components and data flows
Changes adding datastores, model providers or infrastructure a threat model should name
inspect: Tracked *.otm.json files
Other pieces' derived facts for components the model does not name
Noru risks and controls needed to link and reconcile
pieces.caveat: A threat in a model is something someone thought of, not a conclusion; whether it applies, how bad it is and who owns it are the user's.

utilities.name: repo-enforcement
utilities.summary: Install and verify GitHub merge enforcement for the repository-wide GRC workflow.
signals: A request to make GRC or compliance checks mandatory before merge
A request to configure branch protection, rulesets, CODEOWNERS, or controlled debt adoption
A request to detect weakening of repository governance
inspect: .noru/enforcement.yml and its ratchet baseline
The always-running Noru GRC workflow and CODEOWNERS
Effective repository and inherited organisation rulesets
utilities.caveat: This utility administers GitHub enforcement and never writes a compliance claim to Noru; ruleset apply requires a fresh plan and separate confirmation.
